title: Combination Sum
oneLinerQuestion: Find all unique combinations of candidate numbers that sum up to a target with unlimited reuse allowed.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Combination Sum problem requires finding all unique combinations of candidate numbers where the chosen numbers sum up to a target value. Since each candidate number can be reused an unlimited number of times, this combinatorial search maps directly to a state space tree explored via Backtracking (Depth-First Search). By enforcing a forward-only traversal index, we prevent duplicate combinations (such as [2, 2, 3] and [3, 2, 2]) without needing an expensive post-processing deduplication step.

- Step 1: Pre-Sorting Candidates — We sort the candidates array in ascending order. Sorting enables early termination (pruning): if the current candidate exceeds the remaining target, all subsequent larger candidates will also exceed it, allowing us to safely break out of the loop immediately.

- Step 2: Backtracking Function Definition — We define a recursive helper backtrack(startIndex, remainingTarget, currentCombination). 'startIndex' restricts the pool of available numbers to the current element and elements to its right, ensuring combinations are constructed in non-decreasing order.

- Step 3: Base Conditions & Pruning — If remainingTarget === 0, the elements in currentCombination sum exactly to the target, so we push a snapshot copy of currentCombination into our result array and return. If remainingTarget < 0, the sum has overshot the target, so we return immediately to trigger backtracking.

- Step 4: Iterative Branching & State Exploration — We iterate with pointer 'i' from startIndex to candidates.length - 1. If candidates[i] > remainingTarget, we break early due to sorted order. Otherwise, we add candidates[i] to currentCombination and call backtrack(i, remainingTarget - candidates[i], currentCombination), passing 'i' as the new startIndex to allow unlimited reuse of the same number.

- Step 5: Backtrack & Unwind — After returning from the recursive branch, we pop candidates[i] from currentCombination. This restores the array's previous state, allowing the loop to proceed to candidates[i + 1] and explore alternative branches cleanly.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(2^T) where T is target / min(candidates), bounded by the maximum depth of the search tree. Space Complexity: O(T) auxiliary space for the recursion stack and combination buffer representing the maximum possible depth of valid paths.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION combinationSum(candidates, target):
    res = []
    FUNCTION backtrack(idx, current, sum):
        IF sum == target THEN APPEND COPY(current) TO res; RETURN
        IF sum > target OR idx >= LENGTH(candidates) THEN RETURN
        APPEND candidates[idx] TO current
        backtrack(idx, current, sum + candidates[idx])
        POP current
        backtrack(idx + 1, current, sum)
    END FUNCTION
    backtrack(0, [], 0)
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION
